title: Injective sheaves have surjective restriction maps
statement: Let X be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], U' ⊆ U open subspaces, and I an injective O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category; def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the restriction map $I(U)\to I(U')$ is surjective. Consequently, for open U,V ⊆ X and any injective I, the map $I(U) \oplus I(V)\to I(U\cap V)$, $(a,b)\mapsto a|_{U\cap V} - b|_{U\cap V}$, is surjective.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$. Let $P_U$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on $X$ with $P_U(V)=\mathcal O_X(V)$ (acting on itself) for open $V\subseteq U$ and $P_U(V)=0$ for $V\not\subseteq U$, with the restriction maps of $\mathcal O_X$ between opens contained in $U$ and $0$ otherwise; let $\theta_U:P_U\to j_!\mathcal O_U:=P_U^\#$ be its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], whose underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of $P_U$. Define $P_{U'}$, $\theta_{U'}$, $j'_!\mathcal O_{U'}$ likewise. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, the universal property of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_!\mathcal O_U,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P_U,\mathcal F)$, $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta_U$, onto the $\mathcal O_X$-linear presheaf maps. Such a presheaf map $\varphi$ is zero on opens $V\not\subseteq U$, and on $V\subseteq U$ the $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear map $\varphi_V:\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal F(V)$ is $r\mapsto r\,\varphi_V(1)$ with $\varphi_V(1)=\varphi_U(1)|_V$ by compatibility with restriction; conversely each $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ defines such a map $r\mapsto r\,s|_V$. Hence $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_U)_U(1)$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_!\mathcal O_U,\mathcal F)\cong\mathcal F(U)$, and likewise $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j'_!\mathcal O_{U'},\mathcal F)\cong\mathcal F(U')$ (Stacks 01EA proof; the extension by zero $j_!\mathcal O_U$ of Sheaves 00A4).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, the two Hom identifications

proof.text: Let $\alpha_p:P_{U'}\to P_U$ be the identity on opens $V\subseteq U'$ and $0$ on all other opens; it is a map of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and let $\alpha:j'_!\mathcal O_{U'}\to j_!\mathcal O_U$ be the induced map with $\alpha\circ\theta_{U'}=\theta_U\circ\alpha_p$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For $x\in X$ the stalk $(P_U)_x$ is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ if $x\in U$ (the neighbourhoods inside $U$ are cofinal) and $0$ if $x\notin U$ (then no neighbourhood of $x$ lies in $U$); so $(\alpha_p)_x$ is the identity of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for $x\in U'$ and has source $0$ for $x\notin U'$, hence is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] the maps $(\theta_U)_x$, $(\theta_{U'})_x$ are isomorphisms, so $\alpha_x=(\theta_U)_x(\alpha_p)_x(\theta_{U'})_x^{-1}$ is injective for every $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5), applied to $0\to j'_!\mathcal O_{U'}\xrightarrow{\alpha}j_!\mathcal O_U$, $\alpha$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, canonical map and injectivity from stalks

proof.text: Since $\mathcal I$ is injective, the defining lifting property of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] makes precomposition with the monomorphism $\alpha$ a surjection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_!\mathcal O_U,\mathcal I)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j'_!\mathcal O_{U'},\mathcal I)$. Under the bijections of Step 1, $\psi\circ\alpha$ corresponds to $(\psi\circ\alpha\circ\theta_{U'})_{U'}(1)=(\psi\circ\theta_U)_{U'}((\alpha_p)_{U'}(1))=(\psi\circ\theta_U)_{U'}(1)=(\psi\circ\theta_U)_U(1)|_{U'}$, so precomposition with $\alpha$ is the restriction map $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U')$, which is therefore surjective.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, injectivity and conclusion

proof.text: For open $U,V\subseteq X$, apply Step 3 to the inclusions $U\cap V\subseteq U$ and $U\cap V\subseteq V$. Given $c\in\mathcal I(U\cap V)$, choose $a\in\mathcal I(U)$ restricting to $c$ and take $b=0\in\mathcal I(V)$. Then $(a,b)$ maps to $a|_{U\cap V}-b|_{U\cap V}=c$, proving that $\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\to\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ is surjective.

split_report.summary: Split the Stacks 01EA argument into four proof steps. Extension by zero of the structure sheaf is built inline as the module sheafification of the explicit presheaf, which represents sections; stalks of a sheafification and stalkwise exactness make the nested-open map a monomorphism; injectivity gives surjectivity on sections, and the two-open difference-map consequence is elementary. No new nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the 09MR Mayer–Vietoris paragraph's assertion that sections of an injective sheaf restrict surjectively to an intersection, together with the resulting difference-map surjectivity.

tool_uses.why: Its generic ringed-space clause (5) is the stalkwise exactness criterion needed to turn the explicit injective stalk maps of the extension-by-zero morphism into a monomorphism; the unit has no replacement for this general sheaf fact.
Generic topological fact that sheafification preserves stalks, used to compute the stalks of the extension-by-zero sheaves.

lean.statement: theorem injective_restriction_surjective (X : RingedSpace.{u}) {U' U : Opens X} (hU : U' ≤ U) (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) [Injective I] : Function.Surjective (fun s : I.val.obj (Opposite.op U) => (I.val.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom s) ∧ ∀ (V W : Opens X), Function.Surjective (fun p : I.val.obj (Opposite.op V) × I.val.obj (Opposite.op W) => (show I.val.obj (Opposite.op (V ⊓ W)) from (I.val.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V ⊓ W ≤ V)).op).hom p.1) - (show I.val.obj (Opposite.op (V ⊓ W)) from (I.val.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V ⊓ W ≤ W)).op).hom p.2))
